name: up
desc: Tool for writing command-line pipes with instant live preview
why: Interactive pipeline builder with live preview of command-line text transforms; a fun way to learn sed and awk style piping.

brief.what_it_is: up, the Ultimate Plumber, is a terminal UI for building Linux shell pipelines interactively. You redirect any text-emitting command into up, type a pipeline into the input box at the top, and press Enter. up runs the pipeline with bash -c and shows its output in a scrollable preview below. When you are happy with the result, Ctrl-X exits and writes the pipeline to an up1.sh file (or up2.sh and so on if that name is taken). Ctrl-C quits without saving.
brief.why_it_exists: The README says the goal is to help people interactively and incrementally explore textual data in Linux by giving a fast feedback loop while building complex pipelines out of grep, sort, cut, paste, awk, wc, perl and similar tools. The author was surprised no one seemed to have written a similar tool before.
brief.how_it_works: up reads the piped input into a buffer, which the README says is fixed at 40 MB, and runs the pipeline you type through bash -c on each execution. Pressing Enter reruns the pipeline and replaces the preview. Ctrl-S freezes the input and injects a fake EOF, so commands like wc or sort will print results before the input stream has actually ended. Ctrl-Q unfreezes.

commands_seen.context: Example of redirecting a command's output into up to start using it.
Example pipeline the README suggests typing into up's input box; the README shows its output as two lines of wireless and ethernet interface names.

brief.install_notes: Installs with brew install up on macOS, though the README says the author does not have a Mac and cannot confirm it works there. Other routes given are a direct Linux binary download from GitHub releases, the AUR (aur/up), and FreeBSD pkg install up. No runtime, account, or configuration is mentioned. The Homebrew scout notes list one executable, up.
brief.standout: It runs the pipeline you are typing on every Enter and shows the live output, so you can build a pipeline one stage at a time against real data. The README credits Bret Victor's talks as an influence, and points to Pipecut as earlier prior art.
brief.status: quiet. The README is signed October 2018 and calls the project a purely hobby project. I did not see a release date or last commit in the README, and I did not check the releases page, so the exact last release is unknown.
brief.caveats: The README warns that writing rm or dd into it could be dangerous, since pipelines run for real through bash. The input buffer is fixed at 40 MB. Long-running input shows a tilde and needs Ctrl-S to get partial results from commands like wc or sort. The author says the Mac build is untested. Windows is listed as a future idea, not supported. There is no --help yet and no tests, according to the README's future ideas. The README does not name a license.
quotes: up is the Ultimate Plumber, a tool for writing Linux pipes in a terminal-based UI interactively, with instant live preview of command results.
WARNING: Please be careful when using it! It could be dangerous.
I was surprised no one seemed to write a similar tool before, that I could find.

links.label: Pipecut, the earlier similar project the README mentions
